rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods / Field monitoring <U+2013> a 0.2 ha cotton field at Akaltyn was monitored in 2006<U+2013>2007 for soil moisture, ECe, groundwater depth and yield, and SWAP was calibrated (2006) and validated (2007) on these data. Q2: Results (Fig. 3, Fig. 4, Table III, Table IV) <U+2013> simulated soil moisture (RMSE 0.012<U+2013>0.027), salinity profiles and yields (within 5% of measured) were compared with field measurements; Table IV reports WPT (0.66<U+2013>0.75 kg m-3) and WPET (0.52<U+2013>0.58 kg m-3) and the authors state water productivity can be significantly enhanced by better irrigation management since soil evaporation is ~30% of ETpot; Scenario analysis (Fig. 9) <U+2013> with the validated model, irrigation regimes of 175<U+2013>400 mm at 200 cm water table were simulated and ~3.0 t ha-1 is obtained with 250 mm, with only 3<U+2013>5% further gain above that. Q4: Table IV and Figs 7<U+2013>8 <U+2013> the model quantifies the intermediate variables: actual soil evaporation vs transpiration, capillary rise (qbot) as a function of water-table depth, and root-zone salinity under each scenario. Q7: Scenario analysis and Conclusions <U+2013> the 3.0 t ha-1 at 250 mm holds only while the groundwater table is kept at about 200 cm; irrigation amounts must be adjusted at deeper water tables; to reach potential yields leaching with fresh water and rehabilitation of the drainage network are stated as imperative; farmers must apply irrigations in small amounts to keep the water table deep. Q8: Results <U+2013> ECe measurements were available only on 2<U+2013>3 days per season; differences between measured and simulated moisture attributed to profile heterogeneity and observation error; SWAP assumes optimum nutrition and no pest/disease stress (2006 yield was reduced by insect attack); Conclusions <U+2013> findings are representative only of the current soil-salinity situation of the area.
rows.notes: Study supports the claim only partly: WP (WPT, WPET) is reported for the two observed years, and the optimised irrigation amounts and water-table depth come from scenario runs of a model validated on soil moisture, salinity and yield in the same field; WP is not explicitly computed for the optimised scenarios, so the 'high potential for increasing WP' is an inference from the yield-vs-irrigation curve and the 30% evaporation share. Single field, single crop, one method (SWAP); RMSE is a validation error, and the only dispersion mentioned is the SD of measured ECe used to judge model fit, not a measure of uncertainty on the yield/WP result, so Q9 is no. The 'app_scheduling' technology is interpreted as model-driven scheduling per the extractor note; the study does not use an app or decision-support tool for farmers.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). Study is a single-field SWAP calibration/validation with scenario analysis on groundwater-table depth and irrigation amount for cotton in Syrdarya, Uzbekistan.
